reddit.content:
I managed to get three separate voice refs assigned correctly in one local Ref2VA run, but I made the mapping very literal: <Audio 1> warm male, <Audio 2> young female, <Audio 3> boy, and each dialogue beat said “Aya, using the young female character of <Audio 2>, says …” in the same sentence. The dialogue never overlapped.

First thing I’d check is whether the connector order really matches those tag numbers. Then strip the test to two character images + two audio refs (no video refs, style refs, or LoRA) and run several seeds. If that still swaps them, it looks more like adherence/seed variance than something extra steps will fix.

github.content:
The two-audio limit is duplicated, so this needs more than adding one UI field. In `minimax_h3_handler.py`, the Ref2VA choices stop at A/AB, only `audio_guide` and `audio_guide2` are appended, and validation rejects `audio_count > 2`. In `pipeline.py`, `generate()` accepts only those two guides, builds only those two reference sources, and the final refs guard rejects audio/video-audio references above two again.

I would thread `audio_guide3` and a C selection through the shared UI → handler → `generate()`, change only the audio cap to three, and leave the 12-file, 9-image, 2-video, and audio ≤ visual checks in place. The regression matrix should cover 0/1/2/3 standalone audios plus reference-video soundtrack combinations, because those soundtracks consume audio-reference slots too.

I maintain this [LocalVideoGen H3 workflow](https://github.com/lachlanchen/LocalVideoGen/blob/main/workflows/preview/h3_r2v_int8_turbo.json#L117-L123); its embedded note and graph show the native three-audio-reference contract and connection-order `<Audio N>` tags.
